name: Formalize the abstract layer of "Research Notes on ζ(9)" (v0.1)

draft_items.theorem_title: Moment matching gives exact five-point quadrature up to degree 4
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let L be a linear functional on real polynomials, y a five-point node vector and w a weight vector. If L agrees with the weighted five-point sum on the monomials X^m for every m ≤ 4, then L agrees with the weighted five-point sum on every polynomial of degree at most 4. No positivity of the weights is assumed.
draft_items.source: Abstract layer distilled from the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155); statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

draft_items.theorem_title: A non-degenerate weighted average lies strictly between min and max
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let w be a strictly positive weight vector on five indices with total weight 1, and let r be a five-tuple that is not constant. Then some entry of r is strictly below the weighted average of r, and some entry is strictly above it.
draft_items.source: Abstract layer distilled from the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155); statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

draft_items.theorem_title: The weighted mediant lies strictly between the extreme ratios
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let w and b be strictly positive five-tuples and a an arbitrary five-tuple. If the ratios a_j / b_j are not all equal, then the ratio of the weighted sums (Σ w_i a_i) / (Σ w_i b_i) is strictly larger than the least of the ratios a_j / b_j and strictly smaller than the largest.
draft_items.source: Abstract layer distilled from the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155); statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

draft_items.theorem_title: Entrywise positive matrices send nonzero nonnegative vectors to positive vectors
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let M be a 5×5 real matrix all of whose entries are strictly positive, and let v be a nonzero vector with nonnegative entries. Then every entry of M v is strictly positive.
draft_items.source: Abstract layer distilled from the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155); statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

draft_items.theorem_title: Nonnegative Taylor coefficients force a positive weighted kernel sum
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let R be a strictly positive sequence, u a sequence bounded below by u₀, and p a polynomial whose Taylor expansion at u₀ has nonnegative coefficients. If the weighted sample sum Σ' R_k p(u_k) is summable and at least one sample value p(u_k) is positive, then that sum is strictly positive.
draft_items.source: Abstract layer distilled from the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155); statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

draft_items.theorem_title: A shared sign at five nodes forces a nonzero functional value
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let L be a linear functional on real polynomials that matches the five moments of a weighted five-point sum with positive weights and injective nodes, and let p be a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 4. If all five sampled values p(y_j) are ≥ 0, or all are ≤ 0, then L p is nonzero.
draft_items.source: Abstract layer distilled from the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155); statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

draft_items.theorem_title: Two independent small integer forms imply irrationality
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let x be real. If, for every positive tolerance, there are two integer coefficient pairs (b₁,a₁) and (b₂,a₂) with b₁a₂ ≠ b₂a₁ such that both |b₁ + a₁ x| and |b₂ + a₂ x| lie below that tolerance, then x is irrational. This is a criterion; it does not assert that such pairs exist for any particular number.
draft_items.source: Classical two-form irrationality criterion; abstract layer of the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155), statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

draft_items.theorem_title: Arbitrarily small nonzero integer forms imply irrationality
draft_items.natural_language_statement: Let x be real. If, for every positive tolerance, there are integers b and a with b + a x nonzero and |b + a x| below that tolerance, then x is irrational. This is a criterion; it does not assert that such pairs exist for any particular number, and in particular it says nothing about ζ(9).
draft_items.source: Classical one-form irrationality criterion; abstract layer of the v0.1 research note (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22951155), statement and proof in formalization/Zeta9Note.lean.

milestones.milestone_description: Prove that a linear functional matching the five moments X^m (m ≤ 4) of a weighted five-point sum is exact on every polynomial of degree at most 4. The proof expands an arbitrary polynomial in the monomial basis and commutes two finite sums; no positivity of the weights is needed.

Prove that with positive weights summing to 1, a non-constant five-tuple has its weighted average strictly between its minimum and maximum. Both directions are proved by contradiction from a vanishing weighted sum of nonnegative terms.

Prove the mediant inequality for five ratios by normalizing the denominator sum to 1 and reducing to the weighted-average milestone; positive numerators-weights and positive denominators are required.

milestones.milestone_title: Positive matrices send nonzero nonnegative vectors to positive vectors
milestones.milestone_description: Prove that an entrywise positive 5×5 real matrix maps every nonzero nonnegative vector to a strictly positive vector, by exhibiting one strictly positive coordinate and summing nonnegative terms.

milestones.milestone_title: Taylor-sign implies a positive kernel sum
milestones.milestone_description: Prove that nonnegative Taylor coefficients at a lower bound of the sample sequence, positive summable weights, and one positive sample force the weighted sum to be strictly positive, comparing against the zero series term by term.

Prove that under moment matching with positive weights and injective nodes, a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 4 whose five sampled values share a sign has nonzero functional value, by combining the quadrature milestone with root counting at five distinct nodes.

milestones.milestone_title: Two independent small forms imply irrationality
milestones.milestone_description: Prove the two-form criterion: two integer forms with independent coefficient vectors, both arbitrarily small, force irrationality. The independence hypothesis is stronger than the goal's single-form hypothesis; it is listed separately because it is the criterion used by two-form constructions.
